claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

1. **Do you have any children, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? That is, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and other day-to-day expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I look after him and provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually - Alex has been in hospital for a while now. He's been there for a few months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. This is important information as it may affect your Child Benefit eligibility. I need to understand this situation better:

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for 11 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, which is just under the 12-week threshold, your Child Benefit should not be affected yet. However, I need to ask one more important question:

**Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is he in a hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

**Good news - you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the eligibility requirements:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is under 16 years old (he's 8)
- You're responsible for his care and provide for his needs
- Although Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is still within the 12-week allowance period

**Important to note:** If Alex's hospital stay continues beyond 12 weeks in total, your Child Benefit eligibility may be affected. However, even after 12 weeks, you may still be able to continue receiving Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on Alex (such as buying clothes, toys, or other items for him). 

If his hospital stay does extend beyond 12 weeks, you should contact HMRC to inform them of your circumstances, as there may be exceptions that apply to your situation.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
